saved.waits: Saved. The change waits for a certificate for {{domain}}; until then the site stays as it is.
saved.http: Domains saved. The site is served over HTTP until a certificate for the new domains is there.

card.title: Domains
card.domainsHint: One per line. The first one is the primary domain.
card.redirectHint: One per line. They answer with 301 to {{primary}} and stay on the certificate, so their DNS must keep pointing to this server.
card.both: “{{domain}}” is a served domain and a redirect domain.
card.tooMany: A site can have at most {{max}} domains, redirect domains included.

pending.title: Domain change waiting for its certificate
pending.intro: The site stays on HTTPS with its current domains until a certificate for the new ones is there.
pending.label: Pending domains
pending.failed: The certificate could not be obtained yet. The panel tries again within the hour.
pending.checkDNS: Check that the DNS of every new name points to this server.
pending.getting: Getting the certificate. This usually takes less than a minute.
pending.hsts: HSTS is on: browsers that know this site refuse plain HTTP, so changing without waiting makes it unreachable for them until the certificate is there.
pending.changedNow: Domains changed. The site is served over HTTP until a certificate for the new domains is there.
pending.canceled: Domain change canceled. The site keeps its domains.

change.title: Change primary domain
change.intro: The site keeps its name {{site}}, its Linux user, files, databases, backups and settings. Only the names it answers to change.
change.redirectOldBoth: Redirect <code1>{{old}}</code1> and <code2>{{www}}</code2> to the new domain (301)
change.waits: The site stays on HTTPS with its current domains until a certificate for the new names is there, usually within a minute. If the DNS of a new name is not ready, nothing changes and the error shows here.
change.http: The site is served over HTTP until a certificate for the new names is there.
change.redirectDNS: The redirect domains stay on the certificate, so their DNS must keep pointing to this server.
change.dns: DNS: point every new name to this server first.
change.appAddress: Addresses stored by the app, such as the WordPress site address. For WordPress, after a backup:
change.copyFailed: Copying is not possible here. Select the text and copy it by hand.
change.appConfig: Values with the old address in the app's environment or config files, such as APP_URL.

www.title: www redirect
www.legend: Between a domain and its www name
www.toNonWWW: Redirect to the name without www
www.needsPair: The redirect needs a domain and its www name, both as domains of this site.
www.addMissing: Add the missing name first; its certificate is requested with it.
www.noEffect: No domain has its www partner any more, so the redirect has no effect.

saved.toWWW: Saved. The names without www now redirect to the www names.
saved.toNonWWW: Saved. The www names now redirect to the names without www.
saved.off: Saved. Every domain shows the site again.

added.pending: {{name}} is added as soon as its certificate is there. The site stays on HTTPS until then.
added.http: {{name}} added. The site is served over HTTP until its certificate also names {{name}}.
added.done: {{name}} added. You can choose the redirect now.

redirect.title: Redirect
redirect.targetHint: The full address, for example https://www.example.com or https://example.com/new-shop.
redirect.statusHint: 301 for a move that stays. Browsers remember 301 and 308; use 302 while you test.
redirect.keepPathHint: On: /shop/cart?id=1 goes to the same path on the target. Off: every address goes to the target as it is.
redirect.saved: Every address of the site now goes to {{target}}.

proxy.title: Reverse proxy
proxy.targetHint: The address of the other web server, for example http://10.0.0.5:8080 or https://app.internal.example.com. Private networks are fine; this server's own addresses are not.
proxy.targetHostHint: Off: the other server sees the visitor's domain as Host, as most apps expect. On: it sees the host of the address above.
proxy.insecure: Do not verify the target's certificate
proxy.insecureHint: Only for a target with a self-signed certificate in a network you trust.
proxy.insecureWarning: The connection to the target is encrypted but not verified. Anyone between this server and the target could read it.
proxy.saved: Requests to the site now go to {{target}}.

target.enterRedirect: Enter the address to redirect to.
target.enterProxy: Enter the address to pass requests to.
target.scheme: The address must start with https:// or http://.
target.characters: Use a host and a path of letters, digits and - . _ ~ % ! * + , = : @ & ( ) / only, without ? or #.
target.invalid: This is not a valid address.
target.lowerCase: Write the host in lower case.
target.itself: The address points to the site itself.
target.thisServer: The address points to this server.
target.linkLocalMetadata: Link-local addresses (such as the cloud metadata service) are not allowed.
target.multicastBroadcast: Multicast and broadcast addresses are not allowed.
